meta.title: Greeter takes a Name value object
meta.head: feature/name

overview.bigPicture:
`Greeter` builds the greeting text from whatever string the caller passes. This change puts a `Name` type between the caller and `Greeter`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Caller --> Name --> Greeter.greet
  classDef new fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#1a7f37
  classDef changed fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#9a6700
  class Name new
  class Greeter.greet changed
```

Green is new, yellow is changed; the caller is untouched.
overview.why: Passing a raw `String` let callers send empty or malformed names. Bugs showed up far from the call site.
overview.approach: Introduce a `Name` record and make `Greeter.greet` accept only that type. Callers must construct a `Name`, so validation happens once, at the boundary.
overview.howToRead: Top to bottom: the new type first, then the call site that adopts it, then the class it replaces. Docs and the migration table close the report.

glossary.meaning: New value object wrapping a person's name, so callers cannot pass an arbitrary string.

chapters.title: 1. The new Name type
chapters.intro: Everything else depends on this record, so it comes first. It is the type the rest of the change passes around.

comments.text: A Java `record` gives `equals`, `hashCode` and the `value()` accessor for free.
Declares the package of the `Name` record.
